<!--
================================================================================
  Figure Panels : 2K (Pearson correlation scatter), 2L (violin/boxplot)
  Description   : Quantifies and visualises the relationship between glutamine
                  and glutamate metabolite levels across COLOSSUS MSS RAS-mutant
                  patient samples. Panel 2K is a scatter plot with regression
                  line and Pearson r; panel 2L is a violin + boxplot comparing
                  the two metabolite distributions.
  Input data    : 20200902_ColossusResults_Metabolomics_2_tissue_weight_Centre_
                  run_batch_corrected_data.txt  (same file as Fig 2B)
  Output        : 2K_..._COLOSSUS_Glutamine_GLutamate_correlation.pdf
                  2L_..._COLOSSUS_Glutamine_GLutamate_violin_plot.pdf
                  (uncomment pdf/dev.off lines to save)
  R packages    : ggplot2, ggpubr, reshape2
  Authors       : Anguraj Sadanandam
  Note          : Rows 49 and 51 in metab_known_sd correspond to glutamine and
                  glutamate respectively — verify row indices if the filtered
                  matrix changes.
================================================================================
-->

## Step 1 – Load and filter metabolomics data

```{r load-data}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)   # for stat_cor()
library(reshape2) # for melt()

# Load batch-corrected metabolomics data.
# Same filtering steps as Fig 2B — retain known metabolites with SD > 1.
metab <- read.delim(
  "20200902_ColossusResults_Metabolomics_2_tissue_weight_Centre_run_batch_corrected_data.txt",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Remove unknown metabolites (no HMDB annotation).
unk         <- grep("Unknown", metab[, 1])
metab_known <- metab[-unk, ]

# Filter by SD > 1 to retain variable metabolites.
sd_metab   <- apply(metab_known[, -1], 1, sd)
w_sd_metab <- which(sd_metab > 1)
metab_known_sd <- metab_known[w_sd_metab, ]
```

## Step 2 – Figure 2K: Glutamine vs Glutamate scatter plot

```{r scatter-plot, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
# Extract abundance values for glutamine (row 49) and glutamate (row 51).
# These row positions are specific to the SD-filtered metabolite matrix.
# If the input data changes, verify these row indices using:
#   metab_known_sd[c(49, 51), 1]
glutamine <- unlist(metab_known_sd[49, -1])
glutamate <- unlist(metab_known_sd[51, -1])

# Pearson correlation test between the two metabolites.
cor_result <- cor.test(glutamine, glutamate)
cat("Pearson r =", round(cor_result$estimate, 3),
    "  p =", format.pval(cor_result$p.value, digits = 3), "\n")

# Build data frame for plotting.
df <- data.frame(Glutamine = glutamine, Glutamate = glutamate)

# Scatter plot with linear regression line and Pearson r annotation.
# Uncomment pdf()/dev.off() to save.
# pdf("results/2K_20250518_COLOSSUS_Glutamine_GLutamate_correlation.pdf")
ggplot(df, aes(x = Glutamine, y = Glutamate)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#1f77b4", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linetype = "solid",
              color = "#d62728", linewidth = 1) +
  stat_cor(method = "pearson",
           aes(label = paste0("italic(r)~\"=\"~", ..r.label..,
                              "~\",\"~italic(p)~\"=\"~", ..p.label..)),
           label.x.npc = "left", label.y.npc = "top",
           size = 5, color = "black", parse = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Glutamine vs Glutamate",
       x     = "Glutamine (a.u.)",
       y     = "Glutamate (a.u.)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title       = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text        = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
# dev.off()
```

## Step 3 – Figure 2L: Violin and boxplot comparison

```{r violin-plot, fig.width=5, fig.height=6}
# Re-extract glutamine and glutamate (same indices as above).
glutamine <- unlist(metab_known_sd[49, -1])
glutamate <- unlist(metab_known_sd[51, -1])

# Build a tidy data frame: one row per sample-metabolite pair.
df <- data.frame(
  Sample    = names(glutamine),
  Glutamine = as.numeric(glutamine),
  Glutamate = as.numeric(glutamate)
)

# Reshape to long format for ggplot faceting.
df_long <- melt(df, id.vars = "Sample",
                variable.name = "Metabolite", value.name = "Abundance")

# Boxplot with individual data points and Wilcoxon significance label.
p_box <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = Metabolite, y = Abundance, fill = Metabolite)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, outlier.shape = 16, outlier.size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6, size = 2, color = "gray40") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test",
                     label.y = max(df_long$Abundance) * 1.05) +
  labs(title = "Glutamine and Glutamate levels",
       x = NULL, y = "Abundance (a.u.)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Violin plot — Figure 2L.
# Violin shows full distribution shape; inner boxplot shows quartiles.
p_violin <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = Metabolite, y = Abundance, fill = Metabolite)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, fill = "white", outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6, size = 2, color = "gray40") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test",
                     label.y = max(df_long$Abundance) * 1.05) +
  labs(title = "Glutamine and Glutamate levels",
       x = NULL, y = "Abundance (a.u.)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

print(p_box)

# Save violin plot (Figure 2L).
# pdf("results/2L_20250518_COLOSSUS_Glutamine_GLutamate_violin_plot.pdf")
print(p_violin)
# dev.off()
```
